title: The king as a fighting piece

D0.outcome: Explains that in endings the king becomes a fighting piece that should head for the centre or the targets, unlike in the middlegame.

D1.outcome: Told to bring the king, routes it to the centre or to a passed pawn in the fewest moves in a simple ending.

D2.outcome: In mixed positions, decides whether to centralise the king: centralises when queens are off and no mating threats exist, keeps it home when heavy pieces and checks remain.

D3.outcome: Counts a king-against-passed-pawn race and predicts the effect of a bishop or rook check that punishes a hasty king move.

misconceptions: A king in the centre is always dangerous.
Keep the king at home in an ending.
sources: docs/curriculum-map-v1.1.md §3 (END.KING-ACTIVE, merged from Cap, Nimz, EmL)
conditions: Queens (and most pieces) are off and there are no immediate mating threats against the king.
Centralise the king as soon as the endgame begins, for activity and to limit the enemy king's squares.
contrasts: Queens are still on and a rook lift is available to the opponent.
An immediate king move that fails to a bishop check.
The king cannot reach anything of interest.
